name: Mossbridge
unique_feature: a natural granite arch over a ravine with a warden treant rooted at each end
story: The wardens let anyone cross who carries nothing they did not need. Poachers go round; it takes a day.
encounter: sentinels: do not fight them unless you are carrying stolen forest goods

name: The Oiled Stone
unique_feature: a Hearthstone the Woodfolk oil every week until it shines like a chestnut
story: Oiling is tending; tending keeps the note. The forester who forgets it is sent to the Briar for a month.

name: The Hunters' Stand
unique_feature: a high wooden hide built around a living trunk, reached by a rope ladder the poachers pull up
story: The poachers take hart and sell the antlers to Tollmere as Oroth relics. The Woodfolk have said nothing, which is the custom, and also a mistake.
encounter: skirmisher archers above; climb an adjacent tree to reach the platform level

name: Foxfire Falls
unique_feature: a fall into a ravine whose walls glow at night with foxfire fungus
story: The fungus is an alchemy ingredient worth a month's charcoal. Weavers string the ravine after dark.
encounter: weaver ambush from above at night; safe by day

name: The Hart Bones
unique_feature: an antlered skull the size of a house, of no beast anyone can name
story: The Hart-Knights wear antlers in its memory. The clans say it is a giant's dog. The Sayers say it is a mistake in the record.
encounter: a Hart-Knight keeps vigil at the skull; an elite duel with room to circle

name: The Breach
unique_feature: a gap in the Briar where the thorns have withered around broken Oroth wardstones
story: Something came through from the far side and the thorns died where it walked. Ash-wights, a long way from Cinderlea, wander near it. This is where the Briar's purpose becomes a question.
encounter: ash-wights (swarm) far from home; a main-quest clue

name: The Charcoal Camp
unique_feature: smoking turf kilns tended by burners who never sleep at the same time
story: The burners buy anything that burns and sell gossip that does not. A safe camp with a job board.

name: Fern Gully
unique_feature: a ravine so deep it holds mist at noon, crossed by silk bridges that hum
story: The back door to Weaverdeep. Woodfolk lost a whole hunting party here and left the bridges as a warning; the weavers kept them as a larder.
encounter: weavers on the bridges; cut a bridge to drop a pursuer; shortcut into Weaverdeep's lower level

name: The Northgate Stone
unique_feature: a Hearthstone facing the Briar's northern gate, whose wardstone still carries the Circle's chalk mark from 1038
story: The gate the Circle's Listeners went through. The chalk has not washed off in five years of rain, which the Woodfolk take as the gate's opinion of the Circle.
hook: The Circle wants the northern gate opened for a second expedition; Rookhold will not, and the northern gate has no keepers.

name: The Old Gate Stone
unique_feature: a Hearthstone facing the Old Gate, the one gate of the four whose doors still close
story: The keepers of Rookhold swear their oath at this stone with their backs to the gate, so that the last thing they see before they take the watch is the Wold.
hook: Every keeper has sworn facing the Wold; the youngest swore hers facing the gate, and the doors opened that night.

name: The Moot Gate Stone
unique_feature: a Hearthstone facing the Moot Gate, where the Briar is thickest and the Hart-Knights swear their vigil
story: The Hart-Knights kneel here before they take the antlers, facing the gate the Hart of Thorns is said to have come through.
hook: A Hart-Knight has knelt at the Moot Gate Stone three days and will not say what he is waiting for.

name: The Grey Man
unique_feature: a tor whose three topmost stones stand like old men in cloaks, looking west over the Wold
story: The Woodfolk say the Grey Man is three brothers who stood still to listen to the Standing Moot's hum and forgot to stop.
hook: From the top of the Grey Man the Moot's hum is audible, and it has a word in it.

name: Hollin Tor
unique_feature: a holly-grown tor crowned with leaning stones where the Woodfolk hang the unstrung bows of their dead
story: When a woodfolk hunter dies their bow is unstrung and hung on Hollin Tor. There are a thousand bows. None has ever been restrung.
hook: One of the bows on Hollin Tor has been restrung.

name: Wold Force
unique_feature: the Wold Water dropping in a single rope of white down a granite step, with a stone bench cut into the rock beside it
story: Fernhold's foresters settle arguments at Wold Force: whoever can sit longest on the bench in the spray without speaking wins.
hook: Alder Wyke and a Sayer have been sitting on the bench at Wold Force for two days.

name: Blackgill Falls
unique_feature: three falls stepping down the granite stair through a gill so overhung with oak it is dark at noon
story: Weavers breed in Blackgill's dark. The Northwold's woodfolk throw a lit torch down each fall before they go past it.
hook: A woodfolk child fell into Blackgill and came up in the Mere two days later, dry.

name: Barkbridge
unique_feature: a woodfolk bridge of three bark-roofed spans on granite piers, the only covered bridge in Wickmere
story: The Wold roofs its bridges so a traveller caught by rain has somewhere to stand without asking anybody's leave. Leave is not asked in the Wold; shelter is simply there.
hook: A poacher sleeps under Barkbridge's roof every night and nobody moves him on, because that is the custom, and he is counting on it.

name: The Antler Chapel
unique_feature: a roofless hall where the Hart-Knights hang the antlers of every hart they have killed, in the Hart's memory
story: The Hart-Knights' chapel was a woodfolk lodge until the knights took the antlers up. The Woodfolk say the knights are mourners who have forgotten what for.
hook: A knight asks for the antlers the poachers sold in Tollmere as Oroth relics to be brought back.

name: The Antler Boilers
unique_feature: a poachers' camp where hart antlers are sawn and boiled to pass for Oroth relics in the Tollmere market
story: The Hunters' Stand's poachers do their butchery here, as far from the lodges as the Wold allows. The Woodfolk know, and have said nothing, which is the custom and a mistake.
hook: The Ledger of Prices lists Oroth antler at forty marks; the boilers' account book lists it at two.

name: The Sawpit
unique_feature: a sawpit under a trestle where two sawyers have not spoken in eleven years and never missed a stroke
story: Top-man and pit-man, brothers, sawing the Wold's planks for Tamwick's carts. They fell out over a woman who married neither, and the saw has done their talking since.
hook: One brother asks for a message to be carried down the pit to the other.

name: Mossgrave
unique_feature: a woodfolk burial ground where the dead are laid under moss and each grave's moss is given their name
story: The Woodfolk bury without stones: a body under a named moss, and the moss tended until nobody remembers the name, which is when the moss is let go.
encounter: a Warden stands among the mounds
hook: One moss has been let go that somebody still remembers.

name: The Wardstone Line
unique_feature: a line of broken Oroth wardstones running back from the Briar into the wood, as if the thorn once stood here
story: The Briar has moved. The Circle says the Builders grew it further out; the Woodfolk say it stood further in and has crept east for nine hundred years, away from something.
hook: Measure the line against the Briar and settle which way it has moved.

name: Harrow Tor
unique_feature: a granite tor whose top is a cairn of every stone the northern gate's keepers ever cleared from the road
story: The northern gate had keepers once. They cleared the road each morning and carried every stone up here. Nobody has cleared the road since the Chain Years.
hook: The road to the northern gate is clear again every morning, and there are no keepers.

name: The Skarl Bridge
unique_feature: a granite bridge where the Wold's north road crosses the Skarl Water into clan country, a woodfolk bow-knot cut in one parapet and a clan mark in the other
story: The border between custom and blood-price is the middle of this bridge. Travellers pay the clan toll on one side and ask the Woodfolk's leave on the other, and the wise do both twice.
hook: Somebody has been paying blood-price at the middle of the bridge for a death on the Woodfolk side.

name: The Sentinels
unique_feature: three leaning granite stones in a clearing where the wardens gather at dusk and stand as if listening
story: The wardens, the Wold's walking trees, gather here at dusk and stand among the stones until dawn. The Woodfolk do not cut within bowshot of the clearing.
hook: The wardens have started standing at the Sentinels by day as well, all facing the Briar.

name: The Old Quarry
unique_feature: a granite quarry where the Builders cut the stone for the Long Stride, its last block still hanging half-cut from the face
story: The quarrymen's marks are the causeway's marks. Tollmere does not like to be reminded that its famous Oroth causeway came out of a wood it calls savage.
hook: The half-cut block has Oroth writing on its hidden face: the Stride's own dedication, never laid.

name: Countwatch
unique_feature: a squat granite watch-tower on a tor, its walls chalked with the tally of grey patches on the Briar, nineteen and counting
story: Fernhold's foresters climb it every morning to count the grey patches in the thorn. Fourteen at midwinter, nineteen now; the chalk will run out before the wall does.
hook: The count went down by one overnight; the patch did not heal, it moved.

name: The Silked Camp
unique_feature: a woodfolk hunting camp abandoned in one night and strung over since with weaver silk, the bedrolls still in the tents
story: Six hunters from Ormhold slept here eleven years ago and were not found. The weavers have kept the camp as a larder, and the Woodfolk have left it as a warning.
hook: Six hunters' bows are missing from Hollin Tor's thousand; the Wold counts them as hung.

name: The Verderer's Tower
unique_feature: a Woodfolk lookout built round a living trunk high over the High Wold's canopy
story: The Woodfolk's only watch on the east. The verderer counts harts and fires, and the fires have been fewer every year.
hook: The verderer saw a fire on the far side of the Thornmarch, outside the world, and has not come down since.

name: The Briar Nursery
unique_feature: the Woodfolk's briar nursery, beds of Thornmarch cuttings in rows under the rampart and a gardener's hut
story: When the Thornmarch thins, the Woodfolk plant it thick again from here. It is the one garden in the Briarwold and the one work nobody volunteers for.
hook: The cuttings have begun to lean east, every one, as if the sun were outside.

name: The Poachers' Lee
unique_feature: a poachers' camp in the lee of the Thornmarch, deer-hides pegged on frames and a bow-rack
story: The Woodfolk know where the camp is. Custom says they may not burn it until the poachers are in it.
hook: The poachers have gone in a hurry and left their catch: a hart with antlers of bone-white wood.

name: The Knight's Mound
unique_feature: a Hart-Knight's grave-mound in the Greatwood, his antlered helm set on top and grown into the roots
story: The Hart-Knights kept the Wold before the Woodfolk came; the last of them was buried here and the wood grew over him. The Woodfolk leave him a cup of water at midwinter.
hook: The cup was drunk from this midwinter.

name: The Tally Hearth
unique_feature: a Hearthstone at a forest crossing hung with Woodfolk tally-sticks, a notch for every tree taken
story: Woodfolk custom: a tree taken is a notch cut, and a notch cut is a tree planted by the next spring. The sticks are the Wold's only ledger.
hook: The notches outnumber the new trees by forty this spring, and the Woodfolk want to know who has been cutting.

name: The Bark Camp
unique_feature: oak trunks stripped white and left standing, the bark drying on racks for Tamwick's tanners
story: The Woodfolk sell bark, never timber. The stripped oaks are left to die standing, which the Woodfolk say is kinder than the axe.
hook: One stripped oak has grown its bark back in a week.

name: Pellow's Pale
unique_feature: the wall of a Tallyman's deer-park falling down in the Lower Wold, its gate still locked
story: Guildmaster Pellow walled a deer-park here in 996, and the Woodfolk let the harts out through the wall the night it was finished. The wall has been falling down politely ever since.
hook: The gate has been unlocked from inside, with a key the Tallymen swear was never cut.

name: The Foxgill Arch
unique_feature: a natural granite arch over the Foxgill gorge, with Woodfolk railings along it
story: The Woodfolk did not build it and will not say who did; they only put the railings on.
hook: The railings have been cut through on the Fernhold side.

name: The Fallen Firewatch
unique_feature: a Woodfolk fire-watch tower lying on its side in the bracken where the wind put it
story: The Woodfolk watched the High Wold for fires from it until a winter gale laid it down. They left it lying, because a tower that falls has done its watching.
hook: Somebody has climbed the fallen tower and hung a lantern at its top, which is now its side.

name: The Root Hollow
unique_feature: a cave under the roots of a fallen oak in a bank above the ridge road, where the Woodfolk leave a bowl of milk for whatever sleeps inside
story: The Woodfolk say the Root Hollow is where the Lower Wold keeps its bad dreams, and leave milk at its mouth so they stay inside, and nobody has been further in than the milk bowl.
hook: The milk bowl was found full this morning, of something that was not milk, and warm.

name: The Laid Fire
unique_feature: a Woodfolk way-shelter where the charcoal road enters the oaks, a bark-roofed lean-to over a ring of stones with a fire kept laid in it for whoever comes
story: Leave is not asked in the Wold, and shelter is simply there. At every road's edge the Woodfolk keep a fire laid and never lit. A traveller may light it, and before leaving must lay it again as well as they found it, which is the only toll the Wold takes.
hook: The fire has been found lit at every dawn this month, and laid again better than the Woodfolk lay it, with wood from no tree that grows in the Wold.

name: The Masons' Lodge
unique_feature: the roofless lodge where the Builders' quarrymen slept below the Old Quarry, one gable standing and the Oroth masons' marks cut in its door-jamb
story: The stone for the Long Stride came out of the Old Quarry, and the quarrymen slept here. Their marks on the jamb are the marks on the causeway's stones, which Tollmere would rather not hear, and every Sayer who comes to look copies them.
encounter: a weaver hangs in the lodge's one standing gable after dark
hook: New marks have been cut in the jamb, fresh and sharp, and they are the marks on the half-cut block still hanging in the quarry face.

name: The Leave Stone
unique_feature: a waystone at the Wold end of the Skarl Bridge road with a bow-knot cut in its face, where travellers out of clan country stop and ask the Wold's leave aloud
story: The Woodfolk give no leave and refuse none; asking is the custom, not the answer. Clan folk coming over the Skarl Bridge stop at the stone and ask aloud anyway, because in their country a host is asked, and nobody answers, which is the Wold's way of saying yes.
hook: Something answered this week, a voice out of the oaks, and it said no.

name: The Torch Stone
unique_feature: a stone by the Ormhold road above the Blackgill's falls, with a basket of pitch torches kept beside it for throwing down into the gill
story: Weavers breed in the Blackgill's dark, and the Northwold's woodfolk throw a lit torch down each fall before they pass. The basket by the stone is kept full by whoever passes with a torch to spare, and nobody passes without taking three.
encounter: a weaver drops on travellers after dark
hook: The basket has been emptied every night and no torches have gone down the falls; they have been found deep in the gill, standing upright in a ring, still burning.

name: The Silk-Gatherers' Camp
unique_feature: a camp at the lip of the Blackgill where woodfolk gather weaver silk from the oaks at noon, long poles and reels stacked beside the fire
story: Weaver silk is worth its weight in brass in Tollmere and is gathered only at noon, when the weavers sleep, by woodfolk who wind it off the oaks on long poles and do not stay in the gill a moment past the first shadow.
hook: The silk gathered this week comes off the oaks already spun, into a thread finer than any spinner in Tollmere can make, and knotted every hand's length in the same pattern.

name: The Two Countries Bench
unique_feature: a bench of split oak on a flagged plinth at the Skarl road's last rise in the Wold, a cairn of granite beside it, looking north over the Skarl Water into clan country
story: Northwold foresters sit here in the evening and watch the clan fires come out on the fells. The custom is to sit facing north, with the Wold at your back, so the Wold knows you are keeping watch for it and not on it.
encounter: a clanless outrider crosses the Skarl Water into the Wold after dark
hook: Someone has turned the bench round to face the Wold, and the foresters who sat on it that way say they heard the wood holding its breath.

name: The Uncarried
unique_feature: three rough-cut granite blocks the Builders quarried and never carried, standing on end by the road below the Old Quarry
story: The Builders cut more stone for the Long Stride than they laid. Three blocks were left at the roadside, stood on end so they would not be buried, and the Woodfolk have let them stand, because a thing left waiting for somebody is not the Wold's to move.
hook: One of the blocks has moved a stride nearer the Mere overnight, and there are no drag-marks in the moss.

name: The Planters' Camp
unique_feature: a planters' camp at the forest crossing, oak and ash saplings heeled into a trench beside the fire, waiting for the notches on the Tally Hearth's sticks
story: A tree taken is a notch cut, and a notch cut is a tree planted by the next spring: the Wold's one law that is written down. The planters camp here each spring with the saplings and go out with the sticks from the Tally Hearth, one tree for every notch.
encounter: a warden stands among the heeled saplings at dusk, and minds its own business
hook: Every sapling heeled in at the camp has been planted overnight in a single line running east toward the Briar, and they are taller than a man already.

name: The Moss Bed
unique_feature: a tender's shrine on the road to Mossgrave, a flat stone under a roof of bark where the moss for new graves is started and kept damp
story: The Woodfolk bury under moss, not stone, and a new grave's moss is started here, by the road, where everyone passing sees it growing and knows somebody has died. When it has taken it is carried to Mossgrave and laid over them.
encounter: a poacher cuts across the moss bed on the Mossgrave road at dusk
hook: A new moss has come up on the bed that nobody started, and the tenders say it has already been given a name, and not one of them knows it.

name: The Mourners' Fire
unique_feature: a Hart-Knight's vigil fire by the road below the Knight's Mound, a tent and a cleared ring with antlers hung on the oaks round it
story: The Hart-Knights keep the Wold's last knight in their memory, and one of them keeps a watch-fire here through the dark months. The Woodfolk call them mourners who have forgotten what for, and leave them alone, which the knights take as respect. The keeper of the fire leaves a spare spear against the tent-pole, ash-hafted, for whoever takes the next watch.
encounter: a Hart-Knight keeps the fire after dark
hook: The knight at the fire has been seen leaving a cup of water on the Mound at midwinter, which is the Woodfolk's custom, and which no knight has ever done.

name: The Fourth Brother
unique_feature: a lone grey stone by the road like an old man in a cloak, walking away from the Grey Man's tor
story: The Grey Man is three brothers who stood still to listen to the Standing Moot's hum and forgot to stop. The Woodfolk say there was a fourth, who remembered to stop, and has been walking home ever since, a stride a century.
hook: The Fourth Brother has moved three strides down the road since spring, and has turned his head.

name: The Firewatchers' Camp
unique_feature: the camp the High Wold's firewatchers kept after their tower fell; the fire went out when they left, and the cups are still set round it
story: When the gale laid the Fallen Firewatch down, its watchers camped here and kept the watch from the ground for a season, until the Wold agreed that a fallen tower had done its watching. They let the fire go out and walked home. A watcher's bow still hangs from a branch over the cold camp, unstrung.
hook: Somebody has been sleeping in the cold camp and watching the east, and has chalked a count of fires on its stones: fires in the High Wold where nobody is to light them.

name: The Briar Root
unique_feature: a root-cave under a root of the Briar as thick as a man, come up through the High Wold two miles from the wall
story: The Briar's roots go under the whole Wold, and where one breaks the surface the Woodfolk leave it and mark the place. This one arches out of the ground like a doorway, and the dark under it goes further back than the root should.
encounter: thornhounds round the mouth after dark
hook: The root has put out a green shoot, the first green on any root of the Briar in living memory, and thornhounds lie round the mouth as if they were keeping it.

name: The Road Knot
unique_feature: a lamp-shrine on the Fernhold lane where the Hollow's knot-keepers light a lamp for travellers, set in a stone under a hood of bark
story: Every knot lit in the Grandfather is lit from the one before it, back to the coal the women carried in. The lamp here is lit from the Knot-Hearth each dusk, so that the road to Fernhold carries the Hollow's own fire as far as the stone.
hook: The lamp has been found lit from a fire that is not the Knot-Hearth's, and its flame burns blue.

name: The Silence Stones
unique_feature: three stones by the Fernhold lane below Wold Force where those who lost at the bench go to say what they did not say there
story: Fernhold settles its arguments at Wold Force: whoever sits longest on the bench in the spray without speaking wins. The loser may say everything they held back, but only here, to the stones, out of the winner's hearing.
encounter: thornhounds lie up among the stones by day
hook: Somebody has been talking to the stones every night for a month, a long quarrel, and in the mornings the stones are wet with spray though the falls are two hundred paces away.

name: The Antler-Smith's House
unique_feature: the roofless house of the antler-smith who made the Hart-Knights' helms, one gable standing and the cold forge still in its corner
story: The last smith who could set a hart's antlers into a helm lived here under the Hart Bones and died without an apprentice. The knights wear their helms until they break now, and bury them with their owners, and there are fewer every year.
hook: Smoke rises from the cold forge at night, and in the morning there is a new helm on the anvil, antlered, and sized for a child.

name: The Poachers' Cache
unique_feature: a poachers' fire in a hollow off the Moot road, hart hides pegged out to dry and antlers bundled for the carts to Tollmere
story: The poachers take hart in the Greatwood and sell the antlers in Tollmere as Oroth relics. The Woodfolk have said nothing, which is the custom, and the Hart-Knights have said a great deal, which has not helped.
encounter: two poachers at the fire after dark
hook: The antlers bundled for Tollmere were found unbundled in the morning and hung in the oaks round the fire, the way the Hart-Knights hang theirs in the Antler Chapel.

name: Wenna's House
unique_feature: the roofless chalk-cob house of a Vale woman who married into the Wold, one gable standing, her grave inside its walls under a stone lid and a Woodfolk moss
story: Wenna Tamwood came from Tamwick and married a forester, and wanted to be buried both ways: under a Vale stone, so she would be remembered, and under a Woodfolk moss, so she would be let go. Her family did both, and the house fell in round her.
encounter: a weaver has strung the roofless house
hook: The moss on her grave has been let go, as the Woodfolk do when nobody remembers the name, and somebody has cut her name into the lid in Vale letters.

name: The Oil-Carriers' Stone
unique_feature: a flat stone on the Moot road where the oil jars are set down to rest, rubbed with forty years of spilled oil until it shines like a chestnut
story: The Standing Moot's stones are oiled by hand every week, and the oil is carried up from Fernhold in jars on a yoke. The carriers rest the jars here, and what spills is left on the stone, because oil that falls on the road to the Moot is already the Moot's.
hook: The oil jars left here to rest overnight were found empty in the morning and every stone of the Moot oiled, by nobody who had carried the jars.

name: The Hart Count
unique_feature: a waystone on the Moot road cut with a hart's head, notched down both faces by the verderer for every hart counted in the Greatwood
story: The verderer walks the Moot road every autumn and counts the harts, and notches the stone, and the count is the Wold's wealth as far as the Woodfolk keep any. The notches have been fewer every year since the poachers came.
hook: The notches have begun to be filled in, one by one, with pitch, as if harts that were counted are being uncounted.

name: The Drunk Stones
unique_feature: three leaning stones at the bend of the Wold Road where Tamwick's cider carts slow for the corner
story: Tamwick's carts take the Wold Road to the Hollow with the cider, and slow for the bend here, and slop. The carters say the stones lean because they have been drinking what spills for three hundred years, and every carter tips a cup at the bend to keep them from falling over entirely.
hook: The stones stood straight one morning, upright as the day they were set, and had leaned again by noon.

name: The Bread Stone
unique_feature: a stone at the Hollow road's bend where Tamwick's carters leave a loaf for the children of Grandfather Hollow
story: The Hollow buys Tamwick's cider and will not take it without a gift going back, which is custom. So the carters leave a loaf on the stone, and the Hollow's children run down the road to meet the carts and take it, and the carts are welcomed in.
hook: The loaf has lain untaken on the stone for a week, and the Hollow's children say they were told not to come to the road, and will not say by whom.

name: The Burnt Lodge
unique_feature: the roofless lodge of a woodfolk family who cut timber within bowshot of the Sentinels, its walls scorched black and one gable standing
story: The Woodfolk do not cut within bowshot of the clearing where the wardens gather. One family did, for a lodge, and the wardens came through the wood at dusk and stood round it all night, and in the morning it was burning and the family was on the road to Tamwick.
encounter: a warden stands in the lodge at dusk, and minds its own business
hook: A warden has been seen standing inside the burnt lodge at dusk, alone, with its back to the Sentinels.

name: The Foxfire-Pickers' Camp
unique_feature: a pickers' camp above the Foxgill ravine where foxfire fungus dries on bark trays beside the fire, glowing faintly after dark
story: Foxfire fungus is worth a month's charcoal to Tollmere's alchemists, and it grows only on the ravine walls under Foxfire Falls. The pickers go down on ropes by day and dry it by the fire at night, when the trays glow like a village seen from a hill.
hook: The pickers have stopped going down the ravine: the fungus on the walls has started to glow in the shape of hands.

name: The Flood Stone
unique_feature: a waystone by the Wold Water road cut with the height of every flood since the Wold was settled, the oldest mark high above a man's head
story: The rafters cut a line on the stone at the height of every flood, and the year beside it, so that a rafter who wants to know how bad a spring can be only has to look up. The oldest line is higher than anyone has seen the Wold Water, and nobody knows who cut it.
hook: A new flood mark has been cut above all the others, the highest on the stone, and the year beside it is next spring's.

name: The Coppice Round
unique_feature: a coppicers' camp in a clearing of hazel stools, hurdles and bundles of rods stacked by the fire for the carts to Tamwick
story: Hazelwick cuts its hazel on a seven-year round, a different stand each winter, and every stool has a name and a family. This is the year's cutting-camp, and the families who are not on speaking terms camp at opposite ends of it.
hook: The stools cut last winter have grown seven years' rods in one spring, and Hazelwick cannot agree whose turn it now is.

name: The Rafters' Locker
unique_feature: a root-cave in the Wold Water's bank under an old alder, where the rafters keep their spare poles and ropes out of the rain
story: The rafters make up their rafts behind the Log Boom and keep their spare gear in the hole under the alder, where it stays dry. Nobody locks it. Leave is not asked in the Wold, and the rafters have never lost a pole.
encounter: thornhounds den under the alder roots after dark
hook: The spare poles have been taken out every night and put back wet, and the ropes have been knotted into a raft's lashings for a raft nobody has built.

name: The Wall-Watchers' Fire
unique_feature: a forester's watch-fire at the foot of the Thornmarch track, a bark lean-to and a fire kept in all night facing the Briar
story: Since the grey patches began to spread in the Briar, Fernhold keeps somebody at the wall's foot through the night, with a fire, facing it. Nobody has said what the watcher is to do if the grey comes down, and nobody has asked.
encounter: ash-wights wander up from the Breach after dark
hook: The watcher woke at dawn to find the grey patch nearest the fire gone green again, and the fire let out, and ash tracked from the Breach to the cold hearth and back.

name: The Sawyers' Bench
unique_feature: a bench of split oak on a flagged plinth where the ridge road looks out over the Vale, the Sawpit brothers' noon seat, a cairn of sawn-off knots at one end
story: The two brothers at the Sawpit have not spoken in eleven years and eat their noon bread here at opposite ends of the bench, looking at the Vale, with their backs to each other's half. Each adds a knot from the day's planks to the cairn.
encounter: two poachers carry their antlers down the ridge road after dark
hook: One of the brothers has been seen eating his noon bread in the middle of the bench.

name: The Hart Snares
unique_feature: a snarers' camp in the oaks off the Wold road, hides pegged on hazel frames beside the fire and wire snares coiled on a stump
story: The Woodfolk take hart with the bow and nothing else. Somebody from Tamwick has been setting wire here, which is not custom, and the Woodfolk have said nothing, which is. The thornhounds have said something, and eat what the snares catch.
encounter: thornhounds rob the snare line after dark
hook: The snares have been found each morning cut and coiled, and the hounds that robbed them lying asleep by the fire as if it were theirs.

name: The Webbed Lodge
unique_feature: a woodfolk lodge off the Hollow road that the weavers took, roofless, silk hung across its doorway and its one standing gable
story: A family of the Hollow lived here until a winter the weavers came down out of the canopy early. They moved into the Grandfather and left the lodge to the silk, and the Hollow's children dare each other to touch the doorway.
encounter: two weavers hang in the lodge after dark
hook: The silk across the doorway has been woven into letters, and the Hollow's Keeper of Knots will not read them aloud.

name: The Unasked Camp
unique_feature: a camp of Tollmere bark-strippers on the Barkbridge road, stripped oaks standing white around it and bark bundled for the tanners
story: The Woodfolk sell bark and never timber, and strip an oak only when the Wold agrees. These strippers came up from Tollmere with a guild licence and stripped without asking, and the Woodfolk have said nothing, which is custom, and also a mistake.
encounter: two of the strippers keep poachers' bows by day, and use them only on whoever starts it
hook: The stripped oaks round the camp have put out new bark overnight, grey and smooth, the colour of the Briar.

name: The Knight's Challenge
unique_feature: three leaning stones on the Rookhold road where a Hart-Knight stands to challenge anyone going to the Old Gate
story: The Hart-Knights kept the Wold before the Woodfolk came and still believe the Old Gate is theirs to guard. One of them stands at the stones by day and asks each traveller why they go to the Briar. A good answer passes. A bad one is taken up with a spear, if the traveller insists.
encounter: a Hart-Knight stands at the stones by day, and fights only whoever strikes first
hook: The knight at the stones has started letting everyone pass without a question, and saying only that the gate will not need guarding much longer.

name: The Ringing Oak
unique_feature: an oak on the Standing Moot road with a ring of bronze grown into its trunk at a man's height, the bark folded over it like a lip
story: The Woodfolk say a Hart-Knight hung his helm on the oak to rest and never came back for it, and the tree grew round the helm's rim and swallowed it. You can still knock on the ring, and the tree answers.
hook: The oak has started answering before it is knocked.

name: The Verderer's Moss Grave
unique_feature: a Woodfolk grave on the Standing Moot road, a mossed boulder with a staff of antler-hooked ash stood at its head, a verderer's horn hung on the hook
story: A verderer who kept the Moot road for fifty years asked to lie on it, under moss like any Woodfolk, with his horn where the next verderer could reach it. The next verderer has never taken it down.
hook: The horn on the staff has been heard sounding the verderers' call for the road's closing, at noon, with the road open.

name: The Hazelwick Rumour Stone
unique_feature: a broken waystone on the Hazelwick road, its top lost, the stump scratched over with rumours the Wold folk leave for each other
story: The Hazelwick folk broke the stone themselves, the story goes, to stop it pointing toward the Rafters' Camp, and ever since the stump has been where the Wold leaves its news for whoever walks past.
hook: The newest rumour on the stump says the Rafters have cut a tree that was not theirs to cut, and it is signed with a rafter's mark.

name: The Elderhold Charcoal Hut
unique_feature: a charcoal-burner's hut of poles under turf in the wood by the Elderhold road, the clamp smoking beside it and the cordwood stacked
story: The Elderhold smiths buy their charcoal from one burner who lives out in the wood and has never come into the town. He burns only fallen wood, by the verderers' leave, and leaves his sacks at the road's edge on market mornings.
hook: The burner's sacks have not been at the road's edge for three market mornings, and the clamp is still smoking.

name: The Skarl Delving
unique_feature: a square-cut adit in a mossed granite tor, clan timbering at its mouth gone grey with silk, and a tally-board nailed beside it where a woodfolk notch has been cut across the clan's marks
story: In 1031 the Skarl asked the Woodfolk's leave to follow a vein of tin into the Northwold, and the Woodfolk, who give no leave and refuse none, said nothing. The clan cut for two years. Then their spoil slid in a thaw and buried the charcoal path below the tor, and Davy Colley, eleven, who carried his mother's sacks along it, was under it. The Skarl offered blood-price and nobody would take it, because the Wold has no price for a child. They left the delving the same month. The weavers came up out of Blackgill into the dark galleries, and something bigger came after them.
encounter: weavers at the mouth after dark; inside, weavers and thornhounds in the galleries, silk-thieves who came for the silk and stayed, a Skarl exile who would not go home, and the Reel-Mother in the drowned shaft at the bottom
hook: Somebody has been paying blood-price at the middle of the Skarl Bridge for a death on the Woodfolk side, and the delving's tally-board has a new notch every month.

name: The Horn Pale
unique_feature: a Tollmere buyer's stockade of sharpened oak stakes in a Greatwood clearing, antlers racked over its gate like a hedge of bone, and a price board nailed to the gatepost
story: A Tallymen's factor had the pale built three summers ago, by carpenters from the Rafts, as a buying-house for Oroth antler: the poachers bring their harts' heads here, the factor's men saw and boil and seal them, and the crates go down the Wold Water to Tollmere as relics of the Builders at forty marks the tine. The Woodfolk may not burn a poachers' camp while the poachers are in it. Custom says nothing about a buyer's pale, and so nobody has said anything about it at all.
encounter: poachers on the fighting step and in the yard, archers on the watch platforms, and the factor's hired bravo at the fire; two thornhounds kept on chains, and after dark the rest of the poachers sleeping in the yard as the factor's rules say
hook: The price board at the gate buys Oroth antler at two marks the tine. The Ledger of Prices in Tollmere sells it at forty.

name: The Tallying Hide
unique_feature: a woodfolk hunter's hide built high in a living trunk, looking east through the Greatwood toward the Horn Pale, a tally-post at its foot notched with every hart carried past
story: Corra Bracken hunts for the Hollow and has done nothing about the Horn Pale, because the custom is to say nothing. She has not said anything. She has built a hide in an oak where she can see the poachers go by with the heads, and cut a notch in the post for every one, and she has run out of post twice.
encounter: none; Corra Bracken keeps the hide and the count
hook: The tally-post has two hundred and eleven notches, and Corra Bracken has started cutting them where people will read them.

name: The Listening Horns
unique_feature: the cold camp of the Circle's Listeners of 1038, its fire never relit, three brass listening-horns as tall as a man still on their tripods and pointed at the Briar's northern gate
story: The Sayers' Circle sent six Listeners into the Northwold in 1038 to hear what the Briar keeps. They camped here for a month with their horns turned on the northern gate, wrote down what they heard, and went through. Their camp was left as they left it, because the Woodfolk do not touch what is not theirs, and a Sayer called Merel Quill has come back to it every summer since to listen for them coming home.
encounter: weavers come down to the brass after dark; Merel Quill and her porter keep the camp by day
hook: Merel Quill says the horns heard footsteps on the far side of the thorn last night, walking north along the Briar, and a dog with them, and that one of the Listeners had a dog.

name: The Layers' Ring
unique_feature: a low ring of drystone under the Thornmarch where the thorn-layers camp while they lay the Briar thick again, billhooks and gauntlets hung on the wall and bundles of cut briar stacked at the gap
story: Where the Thornmarch thins the Woodfolk lay it again: they bend living briar down and pin it into the thorn, and plant the Nursery's cuttings in the gaps. It is the one work in the Wold done for nobody in particular, and the layers keep a ring of stone at the rampart's foot to sleep in while they do it, because the thorn does not like to be slept beside.
encounter: the thorn-layers by day; thornhounds come down off the rampart after dark
hook: The layers have found a grey patch that is not on the Briar at all, but half a mile inside the Wold, and Kit Laywood will not lay thorn round it without somebody else's say.

name: The Greyed Ring
unique_feature: a ring of old sallows rooted again from one fallen trunk, every leaf and every inch of bark gone the grey of cold ash, and the moss and bracken grey beneath them to the edge of the ring and no further
story: Countwatch counts the grey patches in the Briar, and every one of them is on the thorn. This one is half a mile inside the Wold, in a ring of sallows the Woodfolk used to cut withies from, and it came in a night. The Briar's roots go under the whole Wold. The layers think the grey came along them.
encounter: ash-wights stand in the ring after dark, facing east
hook: A grey patch half a mile inside the Wold, where the Briar's roots run under it.

name: Stave Hollow
unique_feature: a bowyer's croft walled in a hollow of yews under Hollin Tor, yew staves seasoning in racks along the yard wall and a hunter's bow on every peg of the house
story: Every Woodfolk bow is made at Stave Hollow and every one comes back to it: when a hunter dies the bow is carried here to be unstrung, and from here up the tor to hang with the rest. Aud Yewman has made bows for forty years and unstrung them for thirty, and says the second is the harder trade.
encounter: none; the bowyer sells bows and strings
hook: Aud Yewman has unstrung a bow this spring whose hunter is still alive, because the hunter asked her to.

name: The Northwold Beacon
unique_feature: an unlit beacon on a knoll above the Northwold, a cone of split oak stacked on a drystone round, a pitch barrel beside it and a fire-basket on a pole
story: The Woodfolk's beacons are laid for one thing: fire in the Wold. When the Fallen Firewatch still stood its watchers would light this one, and Rookhold's, and the Hollow's, and every forester in the Wold would come with a spade. It has not been lit since the tower fell, and it is laid fresh every autumn by somebody nobody has seen do it.
encounter: thornhounds lie up in the lee of the knoll at dusk
hook: The beacon has been laid fresh this autumn with wood that is not from the Wold.

name: Colley's Hearth
unique_feature: a charcoal-burner's hut of poles under turf below the Skarl tor, the clamp smoking beside it and the cordwood stacked, and a bed of moss by the door that somebody keeps green
story: Orla Colley has burned charcoal under the tor for thirty years. Her son Davy carried her sacks along the path the Skarl spoil buried in 1033, and the Woodfolk bury under a named moss, and there was nothing to bury. She keeps a bed of moss by the door anyway, and tends it, and has never taken the clan's price.
encounter: none; Orla Colley burns and sells charcoal
hook: Orla Colley has started leaving the door open at night, because she says she can hear the boy's whistle down the delving.

name: The Hartswell
unique_feature: a spring the Woodfolk walled in stone for the harts, a trough worn hollow by their muzzles, slots in the kerb for the hart-herds' staffs and shed antlers left on its lip
story: The High Wold's harts come to the Hartswell at dawn, and the Woodfolk walled the spring so they would, and do not hunt within sight of it: that is the oldest custom in the Wold after the moss. The poachers know the custom as well as anybody. They wait in the bracken at first light with their bows strung, because nobody else will be there.
encounter: poachers wait in the bracken at dawn for the harts
hook: The harts have stopped coming to the Hartswell, and the poachers have not.

name: The Stray Thorn
unique_feature: a tongue of the Briar grown west out of the Thornmarch across a fallen Oroth wardstone, the thorn thick as a man's arm and running inland where no layer ever laid it
story: The Wardstone Line says the Briar once stood further in. The Stray Thorn says it is still trying to. A single runner of briar came out of the rampart here within living memory and crossed the Builders' stone, and every year it is a few yards longer, and the Woodfolk do not cut the Briar, so they have not cut it.
encounter: a pack of thornhounds has laired under the runner
hook: The Stray Thorn grew eleven yards last year, and it is growing toward the Listening Horns.

name: The Tine Barrow
unique_feature: a long barrow of the first Hart-Knights below Moot Tor, its forecourt stones carved with antlers, its tomb door sealed with a hart's skull set in the stone
story: The Hart-Knights kept the Wold before the Woodfolk came, and the first of them lie in the Tine Barrow within sound of the Moot's hum, each with the antlers of the hart he would not kill. One knight still keeps it. Kenard Hartwell has sat at its door for nineteen years and will tell anybody who asks that the knights do not kill harts, and never did, and that every antler in Tollmere was cut off a dead one by somebody else.
encounter: a first knight walks the forecourt after midnight; Kenard Hartwell keeps the door by day
hook: Kenard Hartwell wants the antlers sold in Tollmere as Oroth relics counted, and the count brought to him, so he can say the names over them.
